problem.title: Sprint Velocity Drop: Find Responsible Team
problem.prompt: The engineering department's sprint throughput dashboard shows a concerning symptom: completed story points dropped 65% between Sprint 23 (ending 2024-03-15) and Sprint 24 (ending 2024-03-29). The VP of Engineering needs to understand which team is responsible for the decline before the quarterly planning meeting. Write a diagnostic query that identifies which team(s) experienced the largest absolute drop in completed story points between these two sprints, returning the team name, points completed in each sprint, and the absolute difference. Your query should surface the root cause team(s), not just the overall metric.

composite_moves: join tasks to teams and sprints
group by team and sprint to compute total points per team per sprint
pivot sprint totals into columns (sprint_23_points, sprint_24_points)
order by absolute drop descending to surface largest contributors

hints: This is a metric-drop-by-dimension problem. You need to break down the overall decline by team to find which team(s) drove the drop.

Use a CTE to compute each team's completed story points per sprint, then pivot those sprint totals into side-by-side columns so you can subtract them. A window function or CASE expression can help pivot the data.

Build a CTE that groups by team_id and sprint_id with SUM(story_points) WHERE status = 'completed', then use FILTER (WHERE sprint_id = X) aggregates or a self-join to get sprint_23_points and sprint_24_points in the same row. Compute the drop as sprint_23_points - sprint_24_points, filter WHERE drop > 0, and ORDER BY drop DESC.
problem.answer_key:
WITH team_sprint_totals AS (
  SELECT
    t.team_name,
    s.sprint_id,
    COALESCE(SUM(tk.story_points) FILTER (WHERE tk.status = 'completed'), 0) AS points_completed
  FROM teams t
  CROSS JOIN sprints s
  LEFT JOIN tasks tk ON t.team_id = tk.team_id AND s.sprint_id = tk.sprint_id
  WHERE s.sprint_id IN (23, 24)
  GROUP BY t.team_name, s.sprint_id
),
team_comparison AS (
  SELECT
    team_name,
    SUM(points_completed) FILTER (WHERE sprint_id = 23) AS sprint_23_points,
    SUM(points_completed) FILTER (WHERE sprint_id = 24) AS sprint_24_points
  FROM team_sprint_totals
  GROUP BY team_name
)
SELECT
  team_name,
  sprint_23_points::TEXT,
  sprint_24_points::TEXT,
  (sprint_23_points - sprint_24_points)::TEXT AS absolute_drop
FROM team_comparison
WHERE sprint_23_points - sprint_24_points > 0
ORDER BY (sprint_23_points - sprint_24_points) DESC;
problem.rca_explanation: The diagnostic works by pivoting team-level sprint totals into side-by-side columns using FILTER (WHERE sprint_id = X) aggregates, then computing the absolute drop per team. A naive query that only reports the overall metric (SUM across all teams for each sprint) would show the 65% decline but wouldn't reveal that the Platform team's 10-point drop (or in the larger test dataset, Platform's 26-point and Data Infrastructure's 24-point drops) are the root causes. The CTE chain isolates the dimension (team) responsible, surfacing exactly which team(s) the VP should investigate. The use of CROSS JOIN ensures teams with zero completed points in a sprint still appear (avoiding a missing-row bug), and the FILTER clause cleanly pivots without a self-join.

_meta.scenario: a project management tool tracking sprint completion and task throughput

user_solution:
/* notes */
WITH base AS (
    SELECT
        t.task_id,
        t.team_id,
        ts.team_name,
    	s.sprint_id,
        s.sprint_name,
        s.end_date,
    	t.story_points,
    	t.status
    FROM sprints AS s
    JOIN tasks AS t
        USING(sprint_id)
    JOIN teams AS ts
        USING(team_id)
    WHERE t.status = 'completed'
)
SELECT 
    team_name,
    SUM(CASE WHEN sprint_name = 'Sprint 23' THEN story_points ELSE 0 END) AS sprint_23_points,
    SUM(CASE WHEN sprint_name = 'Sprint 24' THEN story_points ELSE 0 END) AS sprint_24_points,
    ABS(SUM(CASE WHEN sprint_name = 'Sprint 23' THEN story_points ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN sprint_name = 'Sprint 24' THEN story_points ELSE 0 END)) AS absolute_drop
FROM base
GROUP BY 1
HAVING ABS(SUM(CASE WHEN sprint_name = 'Sprint 23' THEN story_points ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN sprint_name = 'Sprint 24' THEN story_points ELSE 0 END)) > 0
ORDER BY 4 DESC;
